title: Qatayef Asafiri: Half-Open Pancakes with Whipped Cream and Pistachio
summary: Soft, bubbly one-sided pancakes pinched into cones, filled with whipped mascarpone cream, dipped in pistachio and finished with cold syrup.
equipment: blender or large bowl and whisk
piping bag with a wide plain nozzle
non-stick frying pan or flat griddle

steps.title: Make the syrup
steps.text: Boil the sugar, 60 ml water and lemon juice, then simmer for 5 min until slightly syrupy. Leave to cool completely; cold syrup keeps the cream filling firm.

steps.title: Blend the batter
steps.text: Blend the flour, semolina, sugar, yeast, baking powder, bicarbonate, milk and water until smooth, about as thick as single cream. Rest for 20 min until a few bubbles appear on top, a sign that the raising agents are working.

steps.title: Whip the cream
steps.text: Whip the mascarpone, double cream, icing sugar and orange blossom water if using to firm peaks. Spoon into the piping bag and chill until needed, as warm cream will slump.

steps.title: Cook one side only
steps.text: Heat the pan over a medium heat without oil. Pour in 1 heaped tbsp of batter for each pancake, 3-4 at a time, so each spreads to about 8 cm. Cook for 1-1.5 min without turning, until the top is dry and covered in tiny holes and the base is golden; the soft, uncooked top is what lets the edges seal.

steps.title: Keep them soft
steps.text: Lift each pancake, holes up, onto a tea towel and cover with the second towel straight away. Trapped steam keeps them pliable. You should end up with about 24.

steps.title: Pinch and fill
steps.text: Fold a pancake in half with the holes inside and pinch the edges together from one end to the middle only, leaving a cone-shaped opening. Pipe in the cream and dip the exposed cream into the ground pistachios.

steps.title: Serve chilled
steps.text: Arrange on a platter and chill for up to 3 h. Drizzle with the cold syrup just before eating.

tips: If the pancakes will not seal, they were cooked too long or left uncovered; keep them under the towel and fill while soft.
Batter that is too thick gives heavy pancakes with few holes. Loosen it with 1 tbsp water.
A common mistake is a pan that is too hot, which browns the base before the top sets. Medium heat is enough.
Syrup goes on at the last minute so the pancakes stay soft rather than soggy.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Unfilled pancakes keep, well wrapped, in the fridge for 1 day. Filled qatayef keep covered in the fridge for up to 1 day; add the syrup just before serving.
